# yantrad

> The Yantra control-plane daemon. Every client talks to this and nothing else; no client ever talks
> directly to a managed machine. An axum server with a read-only JSON API over a background
> snapshot, the writes (`POST /heartbeat`, `new`, and `edit`/`up`/`down`/`resume` per workspace), a
> WebSocket that bridges a workspace's session to a browser, and the dashboard itself. It is an HTTP surface over
> `yantra-core`, not a second copy of the logic.

## Source

- [src/main.rs](src/main.rs): resolves its bind addresses from Tailscale, fails closed, serves `/healthz`, shuts down on SIGTERM. Plain HTTP on 7717; TLS is `tailscale serve`'s (`just https`, port 8443) and never this crate's. The set it binds is also what `write.rs`'s authoriser trusts a forwarded address from (ADR-0017), so it is passed to the router rather than re-derived.
- [src/refresh.rs](src/refresh.rs): one background task per data class, writing `yantra_core::snapshot::Snapshot`. The interval is a constant, low enough to keep the ssh masters warm. No request path touches ssh. The agents task also feeds the notifier, once its reading is already in the model. **Readiness is a class on this sweep rather than a handler that runs `doctor`** (Y-168): it is the dearest look of the five, and a browser polling it per request is the ssh storm this module exists to prevent. It runs at the same interval as the rest — `ControlPersist=300` means a slower loop would pay a fresh handshake per machine where this one rides the masters the other four keep warm — and takes `write::term()`, since nobody is sitting at this terminal either (I-36).
- [src/notify.rs](src/notify.rs): when the diff runs (Y-146). A difference between two consecutive agent readings and nothing more — no poll, no ssh, no timer of its own; [`yantra_core::notify`](../yantra-core/src/notify.rs) decides what a difference *means*. **The first look after a start says nothing** and **a failed send drops that notification** — no queue, no retry, no replay, with `yantra-agent`'s `Log` as the precedent for saying the first failure and swallowing the rest. A look that failed notifies nobody, because an unknown fleet is not a changed one. The pass has a budget well under the refresh interval, so a relay that accepts and never answers cannot push the next look out. **The relay comes from `YANTRA_NTFY_URL` and `YANTRA_NTFY_TOKEN`** (Y-147), read once in `main.rs`: an absent URL is a daemon with no relay and not a refusal to start, the token is read from the environment and nowhere else, and the startup line says which of the two it got because a unit's environment is not the shell's.
- [src/api.rs](src/api.rs): `GET /api/{machines,workspaces,sessions}`, read-only. Every answer says whether the look succeeded, failed or has not happened, and how old it is. **A `workspaces` entry says whether the file loaded** (Y-141) — one that did not is in the list under its name with its reason, rather than turning the whole class into `looked: "failed"`. `machines` also carries each machine's latest heartbeat and its age, joined on the node id; `null` there is *never heard from* and is not a beat that reports zero. DTOs live here rather than as `Serialize` on core's types (ADR-0005) — **`doctor`'s own types are the exception**, because its check names and three states are the JSON contract [D2 §3.1](../../docs/design/02-setup.md) already publishes. **`GET /api/readiness` and `GET /api/machines/{name}/readiness`** (Y-168) serve that sweep, and answer the one check the library cannot: `heartbeat` is *present* with its age where a beat has arrived, *absent* where none has since this daemon started, and *unknown* where the tailnet list holds no node of that name — the beats are keyed on the node id (I-5) and a report names a machine the way a workspace does (ADR-0009). The one-machine route is a **404** for a machine the sweep did not cover, which is the machines no workspace names.
- [src/web.rs](src/web.rs): serves the built dashboard from `YANTRA_WEB`, with a fallback to `index.html` so deep links reach the app. Refuses at startup if that directory holds no `index.html`, and answers a 404 that says how to set it when nothing is configured. **A directory that vanishes after that check answers `503` and logs it**: the startup refusal looks once, and a `YANTRA_WEB` pointing into a deleted git worktree left `ServeDir` answering an empty 404 — the deep link's own status — with nothing in the journal. The check is on the 404 path, which the SPA fallback makes rare while the directory is there; the line is said once and again when it comes back (`yantra-agent`'s `Log`), and the daemon does not exit, because the API, the heartbeat and the terminal socket are all still serving. **The default build embeds nothing** (R-24): a build that wants `web/dist` unconditionally puts npm on every `fmt`, `clippy`, `test` and musl job.
- [src/web/embedded.rs](src/web/embedded.rs): the same dashboard compiled into the binary, so M7's appliance is one file to copy (Y-140). Behind the `embed-dashboard` feature, which is **absent from `default`** — the module is `#[cfg]`'d and `include_dir` is optional, so a default build neither reads `web/dist` nor compiles the macro that would. A `web/dist` with no `index.html` is a *build* error here, which is the directory half's startup refusal moved as early as it can go. **`YANTRA_WEB` wins over it and a set-but-wrong one still refuses**: the embedded copy is fixed at build time and cannot be mistyped, the variable is typed by a person, so the fallible half keeps the refusal rather than being papered over (R-23). Nothing in `just check` or `just ci` may turn the feature on and `--all-features` may appear nowhere; `just no-node` is that omission made into a red build, and [`.github/workflows/embed.yml`](../../.github/workflows/embed.yml) is the one job that builds with it, kept out of `ci.yml` because `ci.yml` has no path filter.
- [src/write.rs](src/write.rs): `POST /api/workspaces`, `PATCH /api/workspaces/{name}` and `POST /api/workspaces/{name}/{up,down,resume}` — the CLI's own verbs and nothing more (`yantra new`, `edit`, `up`, `down`, `resume`). Authorised per ADR-0016: the caller's source address is resolved **live** via `whois`, and a node that is not this owner's, or carries tags, is refused 403. A `tailscale` that cannot answer is **503**, never 403 — nothing was decided about the caller. **Which address is resolved depends on the hop** ([ADR-0017](../../docs/adr/0017-the-forwarded-address-is-the-caller-when-the-hop-is-ours.md), Y-118): the TCP peer, unless the peer is one of this daemon's own bind addresses — the shape of a request proxied by `tailscale serve` on this machine — in which case it is `X-Forwarded-For`, which must carry exactly one address or the request is **503**. An absent header is not a refusal; a header sent straight to 7717 is ignored. The verbs that reach a machine await ssh, which the read path may not; `new` touches no machine and answers **409** for a name already taken, returning the created workspace in the body because the read model will not hold it for up to 30 s. `edit` (Y-126) rewrites only the fields the body names — `"startup": null` clears the command, an absent key leaves it, and a body naming nothing is a **400** — and answers the workspace as it now reads, in the same shape `new` answers. It reaches the machine **only** when `machine` really changes, and then refuses rather than strands: a tmux session still open on the machine being left is a **409** (I-30, and `yantra down` clears it), and a machine that could not be asked is a **503** rather than a move (R-23). The refusal is [`edit.rs`](../yantra-core/src/edit.rs)'s; this route only carries it. **`up`, `down` and `resume` map every variant they can refuse with, exhaustively and with no wildcard** (Y-135): **409** where the world already answers and a person changes that answer — an agent holding at claude's trust dialog (I-49), one whose credential the gate did not find (I-44), a session opened as a shell, a workspace that runs something of its own, a `repo` the machine does not have, and a macOS machine with no tmux server, which Yantra will not start there ([ADR-0018](../../docs/adr/0018-the-tmux-server-carries-the-macos-login-session.md) §1, Y-151); **503** where nothing was decided — ssh, tmux, terminfo, a status that could not be read, a `resume` whose two sources disagree (R-23); **500** only for this daemon's own — no state directory, a session id it could not generate. Before this everything but a workspace error fell through to 500, and the dashboard drew a state the daemon had named correctly as *the verb ran and failed*.
- [src/terminal.rs](src/terminal.rs): `GET /api/workspaces/{name}/terminal`, a WebSocket over [`yantra_core::pty`](../yantra-core/src/pty.rs). An upgrade is a `GET`, so it does **not** inherit `write.rs`'s check and calls `allowed()` by name — `up` starts a process Yantra chose, a terminal runs whatever is typed. Frames carry no envelope: binary is terminal bytes both ways, text is control — `{"rows":…,"cols":…,"term":…}` from the browser, required first because a pty opens with a window and a terminal (the `term` is the dashboard's own constant, never a user's — I-36), and a failure reason from the daemon, which a close frame cannot hold. **The stream is never logged** (Q5), and **never buffered**: a browser that lost its socket opens another, and the tmux on the far side draws the pane for whichever client attaches (Y-132). It holds ssh for as long as someone is looking, which the request path may not — and it does so after the upgrade has answered. **The daemon originates a ping every 20 s and ends the socket after two consecutive misses** (Y-134), which drops the `Terminal` and with it the `ssh`, the pty and the tmux client on the far side. A traffic timer would be wrong in both directions — output in progress is not idleness, silence is not death — and the pong is a protocol frame rather than the stream, so Q5 is untouched: a peer that answers is never closed however long it prints nothing.
- [src/contract.rs](src/contract.rs): tests only. Renders every read route and every write DTO into [`web/src/contract.gen.ts`](../../web/src/contract.gen.ts), TypeScript that `satisfies` the dashboard's own types, and fails when the committed file no longer matches — `just fixtures` rewrites it. The seam between the daemon and the browser, checked rather than kept in step by convention (Y-124).
- [yantrad.service](yantrad.service): the systemd unit for the appliance (Y-142). `Restart=on-failure` with a `RestartSec` chosen against systemd's five-starts-in-ten-seconds limit, because `listen_on`'s refusal is the retry condition and a fast-exiting unit would otherwise sit in `failed` on a box with nobody at it; `After=tailscaled.service`, which orders the start and waits for no address. A **system** unit: a `--user` one cannot order against `tailscaled.service`, which the user manager does not have. [tests/service_unit.rs](tests/service_unit.rs) runs it under a real systemd in a disposable podman container, and `just appliance-install <host>` copies it onto a box beside the binary (Y-145, [docs/appliance.md](../../docs/appliance.md)).
- [src/heartbeat.rs](src/heartbeat.rs): `POST /heartbeat`, the write `yantra-agent` makes. 204 with an empty body, a 4 KB limit, strict parsing, and identity taken from the source address rather than the payload. Holds `Beats`, one in-memory row per machine keyed on the node id, overwritten every beat.

## What decides its shape

- [ADR-0005](../../docs/adr/0005-core-logic-in-a-library-crate.md): the logic lives in the library; this crate stays thin.
- [ADR-0013](../../docs/adr/0013-the-heartbeat-carries-only-what-placement-scores.md): what `POST /heartbeat` accepts, why it answers nothing, and why the source address is the identity.
- [ADR-0004](../../docs/adr/0004-rust-for-the-daemon.md): Rust, with axum and tokio. TypeScript belongs to the browser — do not introduce a second runtime here.
- [CLAUDE.md](CLAUDE.md): what is already settled, and what to read before starting — including why there is no `--bind` flag.

## Optional

- [tracker.md](tracker.md): the invariants waiting here for the daemon that does not exist yet — SQLite, scheduling, PTY, none of them exercised by shipped code — plus the ones read off the daemon that does: I-58, `listen_on` runs once, so an address that moves under a healthy process is never noticed and `Restart=on-failure` never fires; I-59, the same supervisor re-arming *the first look says nothing* and swallowing every change a restart straddles; and I-60, a startup check over something the filesystem owns being no guarantee at request time — the only one of the three that shipped code enforces rather than merely records, in [src/web.rs](src/web.rs), and the only one anyone has seen.
- [../../tracker.md](../../tracker.md): M4 is the milestone that needs this. Open decisions that affect it are listed there.
- [docs/vision.md](../../docs/vision.md): what the daemon is ultimately for.
